llm.summary: This looks like a purpose-aligned image-generation skill, but it needs Review because it handles the API token through command-line arguments and uses mutable install instructions.

dimensions.detail: package.json declares NETA_TOKEN as a required environment variable, but furryart.js does not read process.env.NETA_TOKEN and instead requires --token from process.argv, which can expose the token through process listings, shell history, or logs.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and README.md recommend npx skills add omactiengartelle/furry-art-skill without pinning the installer version or integrity, so the executed installer can change after review.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions are inconsistent: SKILL.md documents a --style option that the script does not implement, omits the implemented --ref option, and shows token use through --token. README.md documents --ref and the talesofai domain, but the user-facing skill instructions are less complete.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The inspected code does not install persistence, modify local tools, read local files, spawn child processes, elevate privileges, or perform destructive actions; it submits and polls an external API job when invoked.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The artifact coherently generates images from prompts by sending the prompt, size, optional reference UUID, and user-provided token to an external image API. The README discloses api.talesofai.com as the Neta-related service, so the external calls are purpose-aligned rather than evidence of exfiltration.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending prompts and your Neta/Tales of AI token to api.talesofai.com. Prefer a version-pinned install path if available, and avoid putting real API tokens directly on the command line; rotate the token if it has already appeared in shell history, logs, or process telemetry.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Downgraded from the scanner framing: the README explicitly ties Neta to api.talesofai.com, and the external image-generation behavior matches the skill purpose. There is still documentation incompleteness in SKILL.md around the concrete domain and --ref support.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Supported: the script accepts the API token only through --token and the docs encourage that pattern, while package metadata suggests an environment variable that the code does not actually read.
[RP1] unexpected: Supported as a supply-chain concern: the documented npx installer command is not pinned to a reviewed version or digest.
[LP3] expected: Partially supported but not decisive alone: Bash is broad, but the shipped script's observed behavior is limited to argument parsing and the documented image API calls.
[E1] expected: The external POST and polling requests are necessary for an API-backed image generator and are disclosed in README.md; no unrelated destination was found.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The comment label is inaccurate but low impact; the substantive issue is that token handling is CLI-only.
[T09] unexpected: Supported by artifact evidence: command-line token transport is the main credential-handling flaw.
[T08] unexpected: Supported by artifact evidence: installation instructions rely on an unpinned npx execution path.
